producer_report.summary: Interrupted jobs' build directories are now reclaimed at drain start and before each run. The disk is also checked just before the producer, and a job that fails that check is held as an environment stop. Root cause: a job whose process died kept its `target/` until the disk was already low, and the baseline builds then filled what was left, so the producer started on a full disk. The reclaim removes only `target/`. It applies to jobs that are Dispatched in the records, have no registry entry, are not on the drain's keep list, and whose job lock is free; the lock is held while the directory is removed. A hold before the producer leaves no candidate and no resume mark, so a retry now clears the old hold marker once it has dispatched, and `athena go` on such a job says it is read again rather than resumed. The full workspace test suite passed once; fmt and clippy passed; the policy test passed.

criteria_check.evidence: `an_interrupted_jobs_build_directory_is_reclaimed_at_drain_start` calls `drain::drain` with `RealSteps` on a real Dispatched job (request_on on channel web, then a killed producer). It plants `target/`, `work/main.rs` and kept work. After the drain it asserts `target/` is gone, the work file and kept file are unchanged, the job is still Dispatched with its job record, the `disk       removed build directory of job` line was printed, and the lock is free. Passes in the targeted run and the full suite.

criteria_check.criterion: A new test, run with `cargo test`, makes a job's lock held or its process alive (registry entry) and asserts its target/ is kept, and asserts a sweep before a later run reclaims a newly interrupted job's target/.
criteria_check.evidence: `the_reclaim_keeps_live_locked_closed_and_own_jobs` registers a live `sleep` process group for B, holds C's lock, and keeps E on the keep list; it also closes D. A's target/ is removed while B, C, D and E keep theirs and every work tree stays. After the lock is released and the child is killed, a newly interrupted job F and the freed B and C lose their target/ on the next sweep, while E and D keep theirs. `drain_reclaims_at_start_and_before_each_run` (Stub) asserts a sweep at start and before each run, with the interrupted source `x` not on the keep list. The disk.rs unit test `the_interrupted_sweep_skips_locked_and_kept_jobs` covers the lock and the keep list. All pass.

A Ui wrapper writes the low reading only when the `baseline` line appears, so the dispatch gate passes. It asserts: outcome `environment: low disk` (3.0 GB / 10.0 GB), the producer counter is 0, the job is Dispatched with a job record and no outcome or score, the lines run dispatched then baseline then held, the hold marker has 3 GB free and 10 GB required, status shows the low-disk text, and no line mentions `athena retry`. A direct `go` on the held job errors with the 'read again' text. A second drain with space free runs the producer once and clears the old hold marker. Passes.

open_issues: Send-back reruns of the producer are not gated. The new gate runs once, before the first invocation; a rerun still passes the gate before the checks at the built candidate. Gating each rerun would need `producer_loop` to hand the hold back to a caller that owns `closing`.
The pre-producer test trigger depends on `baseline_stage` printing a line that starts `baseline` just before the gate. If that line changes, the test fails loudly because the producer would run.
A hand-run `athena retry` or `athena go` on an interrupted job while a sweep holds its lock fails with 'already running'; running it again works. This is named in the CHANGELOG and docs.
mistakes: My first disk.rs unit test used `&[kept.clone()]`, which clippy rejected (`cloned_ref_to_slice_refs`). I fixed it with `std::slice::from_ref`.
learnings: `simulated_free` in tests/drain.rs reads `<state root>/simulated_free`, where the root is `<fixture state>/repo`; `set_free` writes it.

`Fixture::athena` uses `plenty_of_space`, so target sweeps do not depend on the real disk. A job's records survive `interrupt` (request_on, then a killed producer, then a reset to before the closing commit), and several jobs can be interrupted one after another.
Retrying a held job that has no resume mark works through the existing interrupted-job path: the next drain reads it again as a new job, with no change to `retry`.
`Registry::reap` removes entries whose process group is gone, so killing and waiting for a test child is enough to make a job count as interrupted again.
desires: Bash allowed no `tail`, so I could not trim long cargo output; a quiet flag was the only workaround.
